sections.category: House lawmakers release the Great American AI Act discussion draft, proposing a three-year federal preemption of state frontier-AI rules

bullets.body: Representatives Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.) and Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) released a bipartisan discussion draft of the Great American Artificial Intelligence Act on Thursday June 4 - a roughly 270-page text meant to gather stakeholder feedback before formal introduction, per [FedScoop - Bipartisan 'Great American AI Act' draft proposes new federal AI governance framework](https://fedscoop.com/bipartisan-great-american-ai-act-draft-proposes-new-federal-ai-governance-framework/). The provision drawing the most attention is a three-year preemption of state laws that specifically regulate the *development* of frontier AI models: the moratorium would block state rules such as California's AB 2013 training-data-disclosure law and part of SB 942 on content watermarking, while explicitly leaving in place state laws of general applicability and state rules that govern how AI is *used or deployed*, per [Roll Call - Bipartisan AI draft proposes three-year preemption of state laws](https://rollcall.com/2026/06/04/bipartisan-ai-draft-proposes-three-year-preemption-of-state-laws/). In exchange for the preemption the draft builds a federal layer: it requires large frontier developers - reported at the threshold of more than $500 million in prior-year gross revenue - to publish a public "frontier AI framework" describing the technical and organizational protocols they use to evaluate and manage a model's catastrophic risks (defined as a foreseeable, material risk of mass death), and it codifies the Center for AI Standards and Innovation inside the Commerce Department with $100 million a year authorized for fiscal 2027-2029 to write voluntary guidelines and assess AI systems, per [Nextgov/FCW - Lawmakers propose AI framework that would preempt state laws for 3 years](https://www.nextgov.com/artificial-intelligence/2026/06/lawmakers-propose-ai-framework-would-preempt-state-laws-3-years/413975/). Reaction split immediately along the preemption line - safety advocates praised the catastrophic-risk and loss-of-control focus but called turning the state-law floor into a federal ceiling a "generational mistake" - which sets up the central fight as the draft moves toward a real bill, and matters directly to every frontier lab over the revenue line because it would standardize the disclosure regime they operate under.

sections.category: A critical prompt-injection-to-RCE flaw in the Langroid LLM-agent framework (CVE-2026-25879, CVSS 9.8) keeps the agentic SQL attack surface in the spotlight

bullets.body: A newly published advisory pins a CVSS 9.8 critical rating on CVE-2026-25879 in Langroid, a popular open-source framework for building LLM-powered applications. The flaw lives in Langroid's SQLChatAgent, which executes SQL produced by the model - and because that SQL is steerable by prompt injection, an attacker who can shape the agent's input (directly via a malicious prompt, or indirectly by poisoning data the model later reads) can coerce dangerous, dialect-specific primitives. When the agent connects with a database role that has elevated privileges such as PostgreSQL `pg_execute_server_program`, MySQL `FILE`, or MSSQL `xp_cmdshell`, those primitives (for example `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM`) escalate from data theft to full remote code execution on the database host, per the [GitLab Advisory Database - CVE-2026-25879: Langroid has Prompt to SQL Injection, Leading to RCE](https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/langroid/CVE-2026-25879/). The fix landed in Langroid 0.63.0, which now defaults SQLChatAgent to a SELECT-only allowlist parsed with sqlglot plus a dialect-aware dangerous-pattern blocklist, per the maintainer's [GitHub Security Advisory - Prompt to SQL Injection leading to RCE in Langroid (GHSA-mxfr-6hcw-j9rq)](https://github.com/langroid/langroid/security/advisories/GHSA-mxfr-6hcw-j9rq). The pattern is the through-line for agentic AI security right now: the same text-to-SQL-to-database path produced the actively exploited LiteLLM proxy injection (CVE-2026-42208), where a crafted Authorization header reached an unparameterized key-lookup query through the error-handling path - fixed in v1.83.7 and recommended at v1.83.10-stable, per the [LiteLLM docs - Security Update: CVE-2026-42208 in LiteLLM Proxy](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/cve-2026-42208-litellm-proxy-sql-injection). The lesson both flaws underline is that any LLM allowed to author SQL must run against a least-privilege, read-only-by-default database role, because the model's output has to be treated as untrusted attacker-controllable input.

sections.category: MiniMax launches M3, an open-weight 1M-context coding model claiming to beat GPT-5.5 on SWE-Bench Pro - but the weights are not out yet

bullets.body: China's MiniMax launched M3, which it bills as the first open-weight system to combine frontier coding-agent performance, a one-million-token context window, and native multimodality in one model. The architecture centers on a new MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) mechanism that sidesteps the quadratic cost of full attention by scoring only selected segments, letting the model reach the 1M-token window; MiniMax says it was trained on roughly 100 trillion interleaved text-image tokens and that per-token compute drops to about one-twentieth of its prior M2.7, per [The Decoder - MiniMax M3: open-weight model with a million-token context challenges proprietary leaders](https://the-decoder.com/minimax-m3-open-weight-model-with-a-million-token-context-challenges-proprietary-leaders/). On benchmarks MiniMax reports 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro - ahead of GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro and approaching Claude Opus 4.7 - and 83.5 on the BrowseComp autonomous-web-search test, which it says edges out Opus 4.7's 79.3. The important caveat for local-LLM builders is that the "open-weight" label is, for now, a commitment rather than a fact: the scores are company-reported on MiniMax's own infrastructure, and at launch the model is reachable only through the MiniMax API and the MiniMax Code agent app, with weights and a technical report promised on Hugging Face and GitHub within about ten days - which, as of this writing, have not yet appeared on the MiniMaxAI Hugging Face org (its newest published checkpoint there is still M2.7), per [TechTimes - MiniMax M3 Open-Weight Coding Model: Frontier Claims, Unverified Benchmarks](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/317532/20260601/minimax-m3-open-weight-coding-model-frontier-claims-unverified-benchmarks.htm). Until the checkpoint ships and outside engineers can reproduce the architecture and license, M3 is a benchmark claim to watch rather than something a team can self-host.

sections.category: Bay Area AI events to plan around now span three tracks: WWDC and the AI Engineer World's Fair, AI-security summits (Confidential Computing, AI Risk, Black Hat AI), and AI-chip events (AMD Advancing AI, Hot Chips, AI Infra Summit)

bullets.body: With Microsoft Build and Snowflake Summit both closed, the still-upcoming Bay Area calendar worth planning attendance around now spreads across three distinct tracks. On the mainstream developer side, Apple WWDC26 runs June 8-12 at Apple Park, opening Monday June 8 with the keynote at 10:00 AM PT and the Platforms State of the Union at 1:00 PM PT, per [Apple Developer - WWDC26 special event](https://developer.apple.com/wwdc26/special-event/); Databricks Data + AI Summit follows June 15-18 at Moscone with 800-plus sessions and an OpenAI-partnered agentic-data hackathon, per the [Databricks Newsroom - 2026 Data + AI Summit keynote lineup](https://www.databricks.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/databricks-announces-2026-data-ai-summit-keynote-lineup-and); and the AI Engineer World's Fair runs June 28-July 2 at Moscone West - this year carrying a dedicated Security track (adversarial attacks, prompt injection, agent auth) among its 29 tracks - per the [AI Engineer World's Fair 2026](https://www.ai.engineer/worldsfair/2026) site. On the AI-security track specifically - the category this brief had been under-covering - the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint with a 2026 program centered on agent security, securing AI workloads, and verifiable/attested inference, per [Confidential Computing Summit 2026](https://confidentialcomputingsummit.com/); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay as a CISO-and-AI-security gathering (moved from its earlier June slot), per [SecurityWeek - AI Risk Summit, August 11-12](https://www.securityweek.com/securityweek-to-host-ai-risk-summit-august-11-12-at-the-ritz-carlton-half-moon-bay/); and in Las Vegas, Black Hat USA (August 1-6, with an AI Summit day) and DEF CON 34's AI Village (August 6-9) anchor the agentic-AI red-teaming calendar, per [Black Hat USA 2026](https://blackhat.com/us-26/) and [DEF CON](https://defcon.org/), with OWASP Global AppSec USA returning to San Francisco November 2-6. Zenity - whose May 27 SF AI Agent Security Summit (the practitioner-led format this brief should track) just wrapped - has confirmed a global expansion to New York, London, and APAC, though dates are not yet published and are worth monitoring, per [Zenity - AI Agent Security Summit 2026](https://zenity.io/resources/events/ai-agent-security-summit-2026). On the AI-chip and hardware track, AMD's Advancing AI 2026 data-center-GPU launch event runs July 22-23 at Moscone SF, per [AMD - Advancing AI](https://www.amd.com/en/corporate/events/advancing-ai.html); Hot Chips 2026 (HC38) takes Stanford August 23-25 for its annual silicon-architecture deep dives, per [Hot Chips 2026](https://hotchips.org/); and the AI Infra Summit (formerly the AI Hardware & Edge AI Summit) runs September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center, per [AI Infra Summit 2026](https://www.ai-infra-summit.com/). Further out, GitHub Universe returns to Fort Mason October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas, with re:Invent registration opening June 16.
